q: 269. Critical path moves along the activities having total float?
explain: By definition, the critical path consists of activities with zero total float.

q: 270. Crashing is:
explain: Crashing specifically refers to reducing the duration of the project/activity by applying additional resources.

q: 271. The final means of dispute resolution is
explain: Litigation (court proceedings) is generally regarded as the final/ultimate means of dispute resolution when other methods fail.

q: 272. Critical path method is an effective and powerful method of assessing
options: What tasks must be carried out
Where parallel activities can be performed
The shortest time in which you can complete a project
explain: CPM effectively assesses required tasks, parallel work opportunities, and minimum completion time - all of the above.

q: 273. In PERT (Programme Evaluation & Review Technique) analysis the duration of the activities is taken as:
explain: PERT uses the expected mean time (calculated from the three time estimates) as the duration for scheduling calculations.

q: 274. The most popular type of organization used for civil engineering construction is:
explain: Line and staff organization, combining direct authority with specialist support, is the most popular structure in civil engineering construction.

q: 275. Force Majeure in a contract is:
options: Occurrence of an act beyond the control of both the parties in contract agreement
Preventing both parties to perform the respective obligation agreed
explain: Force majeure encompasses both the occurrence of an uncontrollable event and its effect of preventing both parties from performing their obligations - both A and B.

q: 276. Technical audit of a project may be carried out at the stage:
explain: A technical audit can be conducted at any stage - preparation, procurement, implementation, or post-implementation - covering all of the above.

q: 277. The total float for any activity along the critical path in CPM is:
explain: Activities on the critical path always have zero total float, by definition.

q: 278. Critical path method (CPM) requires:
explain: CPM uses a single deterministic time estimate for each activity, unlike PERT's three estimates.

q: 279. The conception of idea for any construction work is the responsibility of:
explain: but as per book b The owner originates the idea/need for a construction project, initiating the process before engineers or contractors get involved.

q: 280. Motive of private sector for the implementation of the project is to maximize profit while the motive of public sector for the implementation of the project is:
options: Raise the living standard of the people
explain: Public sector projects aim primarily at social welfare - raising the living standard of people - rather than profit maximization like the private sector.

q: 281. CPM stand for:
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method.

q: 282. A bar chart is drawn for:
explain: A bar chart plots time against activities, with bar length representing each activity's duration.

q: 283. The progress monitoring process may be sketched as:
options: Base line data → comparison → analysis → action
explain: Progress monitoring logically flows from establishing baseline data, comparing actual vs planned, analyzing deviations, then taking corrective action.

q: 284. Site order book is used for recording
explain: The site order book records instructions given by the executive engineer to site personnel/contractor.

q: 285. In case of procurement of services
options: both are opened at the same time
no financial and technical proposals are needed
explain: In consultancy/service procurement, the technical proposal is opened and evaluated first, followed by the financial proposal of qualifying bidders.

q: 286. A CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is differences in the planned and actual performance
explain: Network updating is done whenever a deviation is found between planned and actual performance, requiring revision.

q: 287. In PERT, optimistic time represents the following time taken by an activity.
options: expected or average time taken when the activity is repeated several times
time taken if there is delay at every stage except due to natural calamities
minimum possible time taken under ideal conditions
most likely time taken under normal conditions
explain: Optimistic time represents the minimum possible duration an activity would take assuming everything goes ideally well.

q: 288. Which of the following regarding material management is false?
options: materials stored on the site are property of the client and not of the contractor
material for critical activities must be ordered as soon as the contract is awarded
minimum possible time taken under ideal conditions
most likely time taken under normal conditions
explain: Materials brought to site by the contractor generally remain the contractor's property until incorporated into the permanent works (or as per contract terms), making this statement false.

q: 289. Which of the following is an indirect cost in construction work?
options: cost of labour to erect forms
cost of that can be attributed to any single task
explain: Overhead costs (administrative, supervisory) are indirect costs, not directly tied to a specific work item, unlike labour or subcontracted task-specific costs.

q: 290. PERT stands for
options: Pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Programme Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 291. A contractor's role in construction includes:
explain: Maintaining safety at the construction site is a core responsibility of the contractor, unlike payment/certification which are the client/engineer's roles.

q: 292. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: Completion of an activity is marked by an event, represented as a node/connector point - all of above apply.

q: 293. Latest finish time CPM technique is indicated by a:
explain: In many CPM notations, latest finish time is indicated in a rectangular box associated with the node.

q: 294. Negative slack occurs:
options: When latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
When events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack typically results from a deficiency of resources causing schedule delays beyond the allowable time.

q: 295. Which of the followings should be practiced first if a dispute arises in a contract?
explain: Amicable settlement (direct negotiation between parties) is typically the first step attempted before escalating to mediation, adjudication, or arbitration.

q: 296. A quality assurance plan is prepared by
explain: The contractor is responsible for preparing the quality assurance plan for the works to be executed.

q: 297. Float may be defined as the difference between
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and time required to complete the activity
explain: Float can be equivalently expressed via any of these differences (LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or available-required time) - all of the above are valid definitions.

q: 298. Construction team in a project consists of
explain: The construction team comprises the owner, engineer/architect, and contractor collectively - all of the above.

q: 299. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents:
explain: The critical path represents the minimum time required to complete the entire project.

q: 300. Gantt chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart plots activities against time, similar to a standard bar chart.

q: 301. Slack time refers to
explain: Slack time is a term specifically associated with events in network analysis (PERT terminology).

q: 302. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for:
explain: BUT AS PER BOOK C .PERT is a scheduling/planning technique, not related to tender inviting, opening, or awarding processes - hence none of the above.

q: 303. Frederick W. Taylor introduced a system of working known as
explain: F.W. Taylor introduced functional organization, dividing work among specialized functional supervisors.

q: 304. Bidding document is prepared
explain: Bidding documents must be prepared and finalized before the tender notice is published to bidders.

q: 305. What is done in "quality control"?
explain: Quality control involves both detecting defects and taking preventive measures to avoid future non-conformance.

q: 306. The Earned Value Technique in construction management is also known as
explain: The Earned Value Technique tracks project performance using cumulative cost/progress plots, commonly referred to as the S-curve method.

q: 307. Amicable settlement means
explain: Amicable settlement refers to a dispute being resolved directly and mutually by the two contracting parties themselves, without external intervention.

q: 308. When float or slack of an activity is positive, it represents
explain: Positive float indicates spare time is available for the activity, implying flexibility/availability of extra time (and by extension resources) without impacting overall completion.

q: 309. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is called
explain: The network diagram is the standard pictorial representation depicting a project's activities and events with their interrelationships.

q: 310. Procurement of services means
explain: Procurement of services typically refers to hiring consultants or service providers for the required expertise.

q: 311. "Fraudulent Practice" means
options: The offering, giving, receiving of anything of value of influence the action of a public official in the procurement process
Misrepresentation of facts to influence a procurement process
explain: Fraudulent practice covers both improper inducement of officials and misrepresentation of facts - both a and b.

q: 312. Contractor's prequalification is required for:
explain: Prequalification is required specifically for major and specialized works needing verified contractor capability.

q: 313. Which action does not fall under the principle of public procurement?
options: Procurement should be economic and efficient
Procurement should be always at lowest cost
Information and equal opportunities to all
explain: Public procurement principles emphasize value for money and efficiency, not simply the absolute lowest cost, which can compromise quality/responsiveness.

q: 314. Time extension may need to be granted due to
explain: Time extensions can be warranted by force majeure events as well as delays caused by the purchaser/employer - both a and b.

q: 315. Ratio analysis of a construction firm is used for analysis by:
explain: Ratio analysis is fundamentally a tool of financial analysis, used to assess a firm's financial health and performance.

q: 316. Inventory management is related to
options: Inventory of direct and indirect costs
explain: Inventory management deals specifically with materials/stock control, falling under material management.

q: 317. Final technical authority of a project lies with
explain: The Chief Engineer holds the final and highest technical authority over a project in the typical hierarchical engineering setup.

q: 318. The object of technical planning, is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
explain: Technical planning covers preparing specifications, estimates, and initiating resource procurement - all of the above.

q: 319. While filling the tender for any work, the contractor considers
explain: A contractor considers site conditions, material availability, and labour availability while preparing a tender bid - all of the above.

q: 320. In order to balance the needs of the many stakeholders involved in a project, the most desirable method to achieve resolution of conflicts would be:
explain: Compromise is generally the most desirable method to balance and resolve conflicting stakeholder interests fairly.

q: 321. Contingencies should be justified
options: Explicitly, in advance of committing to the budget
Implicitly, to allow for a management reserve
At the time the budget is prepared
explain: Good practice requires contingencies to be explicitly justified and documented in advance, before the budget is committed, ensuring transparency.

q: 322. A fundamental tenet of modern quality management holds that quality is most likely to be achieved by:
options: Striving to do the best job possible
explain: Modern quality management philosophy emphasizes building quality into the plan and process from the start, rather than relying on final inspection.

q: 323. Inputs used during scope planning include all of the following except
explain: Scope planning inputs typically include the project charter, product description, and constraints, but detailed budget/cost analysis is not a direct input to scope planning.

q: 324. The decomposition process is a technique used to construct a:
explain: Decomposition is the technique of breaking down project scope into smaller components to build a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS).

q: 325. The first topic to address in a project kickoff meeting is:
explain: A kickoff meeting typically begins by establishing roles and responsibilities among the project team before diving into plans and schedules.

q: 326. A Work Breakdown Structure numbering system should allow project staff to
options: Identify the level at which individual WBS elements are found
Estimate the costs of WBS elements
explain: A WBS numbering system's primary purpose is to indicate the hierarchical level at which each element resides within the structure.

q: 327. The most crucial time for project risk assessment is
explain: Risk assessment is most crucial during the planning phase, allowing proactive identification and mitigation before execution begins.

q: 328.Including a contingency reserve in the project budget is intended to
options: Reduce the probability of scope changes
Increase the effectiveness of scope controls
Reduce the probability of a cost overrun
Increase the effectiveness of cost controls
explain: A contingency reserve is specifically included to buffer against unforeseen costs, reducing the probability of a cost overrun.

q: 329. A surety bond issued by an insurance company or a bank that provides legal guarantee to the owner or employer that the bidder will sign the contract if it is awarded to him is called
explain: Bid security is the surety bond guaranteeing that the successful bidder will sign the contract if awarded.

q: 330. A project has three independent critical paths A, B and C. To reduce the project length, we have to shorten
options: The activities of A, B and C
explain: When multiple independent critical paths exist, shortening the project duration requires reducing activities on all of them simultaneously (A, B, and C).

q: 331. Major characteristics of project is
options: defined life span with a beginning and end
specific time, cost and performance requirement
explain: A project is characterized by a defined objective, a distinct life span, and specific time/cost/performance requirements - all of the above.

q: 332. Any variation to a contract should be
options: fully considered (including the impact and risk)
explain: Proper contract variation management requires full consideration of impact/risk, documentation, and formal approval - all of the above.

q: 333. When actual cost of construction plus certain profit is paid to the contractor then such a contract is known as
explain: A cost-plus-percentage contract pays the contractor actual costs incurred plus an agreed percentage as profit.

q: 334. A contractor can start the construction works with following the receipt of
explain: The 'notice to proceed' is the formal authorization document that allows the contractor to commence construction works.

q: 335. For procurement of works upto 2 million Rs, by which of the following method of procurement is considered?
options: by direct labour or direct negotiation
explain: Works valued up to Rs. 2 million are procured through the sealed quotation method as per procurement regulations.
